pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

1	# wordstat: Interface Contract
2	
3	## Constraints
4	
5	- **Stack:** Python >=3.11, standard library only; pytest for tests only.
6	- **Package location:** `wordstat/` at repo root (flat layout, no `src/`).
7	- **Entry point:** `python -m wordstat ...` run from repo root.
8	
9	## Functional requirements
10	
11	- **R1** `python -m wordstat --help` exits 0.
12	- **R2** `python -m wordstat [--json] [--top N] FILE` reads exactly one file, decoded as UTF-8 with an optional BOM (`utf-8-sig`). stdin is never read.
13	- **R3** Counts, computed on the decoded text:
14	  - `lines` = `len(text.splitlines())`
15	  - `words` = number of matches of `[a-z0-9]+` in `text.lower()`
16	  - `chars` = `len(text)` (code points, BOM excluded)
17	- **R4** `top` lists the `N` most frequent words (same tokens as R3), ordered by count descending, then word ascending. `--top` defaults to 3. Fewer than `N` distinct words lists all of them.
18	- **R5** Default output is the text format; `--json` selects the JSON format.
19	- **R6** Output is deterministic: UTF-8, `\n` line endings, no locale use. stdout is reconfigured to `encoding="utf-8", newline="\n"`.
20	
21	## Interface contract
22	
23	### Command
24	
25	```
26	python -m wordstat [--json] [--top N] FILE
27	```
28	
29	- argparse `prog` is `wordstat`.
30	- `--top` must be an integer >= 1, else usage error.
31	
32	### Text format
33	
34	Exactly four lines, each ending in `\n`:
35	
36	```
37	lines: <lines>
38	words: <words>
39	chars: <chars>
40	top: <word>=<count> <word>=<count> ...
41	```
42	
43	With no words, the last line is `top:` with no trailing space.
44	
45	### JSON format
46	
47	One line: the result of `json.dumps(obj)` with default separators, followed by `\n`, where `obj` has keys in this order:
48	
49	```
50	{"lines": <int>, "words": <int>, "chars": <int>, "top": [{"word": <str>, "count": <int>}, ...]}
51	```
52	
53	### Exit codes and errors
54	
55	Errors print one line to stderr, prefix `wordstat: error: `, and leave stdout empty. `<path>` is the FILE argument exactly as given.
56	
57	| Condition | Exit | stderr (after prefix) |
58	|---|---|---|
59	| File missing, a directory, or unreadable | 3 | `<path>: cannot read file` |
60	| Not valid UTF-8 | 3 | `<path>: not valid UTF-8` |
61	| Usage error (missing FILE, unknown flag, bad `--top`) | 2 | argparse default; the last stderr line must match `^wordstat: error: ` |
62	
63	Exit 0 on success, including an empty file. Exit 1 is reserved for unexpected internal errors.
64	
65	## Example
66	
67	`sample.txt` (UTF-8, `\n` endings):
68	
69	```
70	The cat sat.
71	The cat ran!
72	A dog.
73	```
74	
75	`python -m wordstat sample.txt` → exit 0, stdout:
76	
77	```
78	lines: 3
79	words: 8
80	chars: 33
81	top: cat=2 the=2 a=1
82	```
83	
84	`python -m wordstat --json --top 2 sample.txt` → exit 0, stdout:
85	
86	```
87	{"lines": 3, "words": 8, "chars": 33, "top": [{"word": "cat", "count": 2}, {"word": "the", "count": 2}]}
88	```
89

1	Build `wordstat`, a tiny Python command-line tool that reads one UTF-8 text file and prints its line, word and character counts plus its most frequent words. It must run as `python -m wordstat FILE` from the repository root using only the Python 3.11+ standard library. Output is a short text summary by default or one line of JSON with `--json`; `--top N` sets how many frequent words to show. Output must be byte-for-byte deterministic on Windows, macOS and Linux. Bad input must fail cleanly with a clear message on stderr and a specific exit code, never a traceback. The full interface contract is in `contract.md`; include pytest tests for your implementation.

## Key findings

1. **Repository is greenfield — zero Python code.** The only tracked content is `brief.md`, `contract.md`, and `.gitignore` (seed commit `d06eb6d`, "seed: brief and contract"). The single untracked item is `docs/spec-001-feature/handoff.md` (confirmed by `git status` snapshot: `?? docs/`). No `*.py`, no package, no tests exist anywhere.

3. **No agent/convention files exist.** No `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, or `README*` at any depth (verified by targeted glob). The `AGENTS.md` referenced by my system prompt is the workflow glossary in the parent tooling, not a file in this repo — there is no in-repo convention document to follow. The only conventions are the constraints inside `contract.md`.

4. **`.gitignore` has exactly one pattern: `__pycache__/`** (`C:\repos\c0-claudex-001\eval-c0-wordstat-20261025T183455Z\.gitignore`). It does **not** ignore `.pytest_cache/`, `*.pyc`, venvs, OS cruft (`Thumbs.db` is a realistic risk on this Windows host), or build artifacts. `.git/info/exclude` is the untouched git default (commented C-oriented examples only).

5. **`contract.md` is authoritative and highly specific** (`C:\repos\c0-claudex-001\eval-c0-wordstat-20261025T183455Z\contract.md`, lines 3–7 for stack constraints, 9–20 for functional requirements R1–R6, 21–64 for the interface contract, 65–88 for the worked example). It mandates: Python >=3.11 stdlib-only (pytest allowed for tests only), flat `wordstat/` at repo root (explicitly **no** `src/` layout), entry via `python -m wordstat` run from repo root, argparse with `prog="wordstat"`, exact exit codes (0/1/2/3), exact error prefix `wordstat: error: `, `utf-8-sig` input decode, `utf-8`/`\n` deterministic stdout via reconfigure, and exact text/JSON output formats.

6. **The `docs/spec-001-feature/` folder holds only a stale handoff from a blocked run.** `handoff.md` records that an earlier run died on permission-denied reads of the `geeky-orchestration` plugin's `SKILL.md`/`AGENTS.md` and that no workflow stage executed. Per that file the prior run did not write code, specs, or plans — and my own tree scan independently confirms nothing else was left behind. It claims "the only change is this `handoff.md`, uncommitted," which matches the `?? docs/` git status.

7. **Exact integration points for a flat `wordstat/` package (all currently missing, all must be created):**
   - `wordstat/__init__.py` — package marker (possibly version-only).
   - `wordstat/__main__.py` — the `python -m wordstat` entry point; this is the module `python -m` resolves from repo root.
   - `wordstat/cli.py` (or similar) — argparse setup with `prog="wordstat"`, stdout reconfigure, error/exit-code handling.
   - `tests/` at repo root (no competing convention exists; flat-layout projects typically keep `tests/` sibling to the package) — plus `tests/conftest.py` if shared fixtures/`tmp_path` helpers are wanted.
   - Pytest invocation will create `.pytest_cache/` at repo root; `__pycache__/` inside `wordstat/` and `tests/` is already covered by the existing `.gitignore` pattern (it matches at any depth), but `.pytest_cache/` is **not** covered and will show up as untracked noise.
   - No `pyproject.toml`/`pytest.ini` is required for `pytest` to discover `tests/test_*.py` with default config; if the spec wants non-default markers or `pythonpath`, a minimal `pytest.ini` or `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` would be the first such file in the repo.

## Constraints discovered

- Stack is fixed by `contract.md`: Python >=3.11, standard library only; pytest is permitted for tests only — no third-party runtime deps, no `requests`, no `click`/`rich`.
- Package location and invocation are fixed: flat `wordstat/` at repo root, no `src/` layout, run as `python -m wordstat ...` **from the repo root** (this is what makes `wordstat/` importable without installation).
- `utf-8-sig` for file reads, UTF-8 + `\n` for stdout, `stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")` for determinism across platforms (a Windows-hosted repo makes this load-bearing — default Windows console encoding would otherwise corrupt output).
- Exact output formats, key order in the JSON object, `top:` line with no trailing space when empty, tie-break (count desc, then word asc), and `--top` default of 3 are all normative in the contract; tests and implementation cannot reinterpret them.
- Exit codes are reserved: 2 = usage (argparse default), 3 = I/O or UTF-8 errors, 1 = reserved for unexpected internal errors, 0 = success including empty file. Errors go to stderr with the `wordstat: error: ` prefix and stdout must stay empty. Usage errors must still end stderr with a line matching `^wordstat: error: `.
- argparse `prog` must be exactly `wordstat`.
- The workflow convention reflected in `docs/spec-001-feature/handoff.md` is that `docs/spec-001-feature/` is the feature folder for this work and that `contract.md` stays authoritative.

## Recommendations

1. Put the CLI entry at `wordstat/__main__.py` delegating to a `main()` in `wordstat/cli.py` (or `core.py`) so the counting logic is unit-testable without running the module; keep pure functions for `lines`/`words`/`chars`/`top` computation per R3–R4 so tests can assert them directly.
2. Place tests in `tests/` at repo root with `test_*.py` names (pytest default discovery needs no config file). 4. Keep output construction centralized (one function for text format, one for JSON) so the "exactly four lines / one JSON line + `\n`" rules and the no-trailing-space `top:` case live in one place rather than being assembled ad hoc.
5. Explicitly reconfigure stdout (`encoding="utf-8", newline="\n"`) and never rely on locale or `print` defaults, since the contract requires byte-identical output across platforms and this machine is Windows.
6. Do not introduce a `pyproject.toml`/`setup.py` unless the spec needs it — the contract only requires `python -m wordstat` from repo root, and a flat layout satisfies that with zero packaging; adding packaging would be scope creep relative to the seed conventions.
